clue.text: You'll hear it said they're too in love

definitions.text: You'll hear it said they're too in love

parts.words: You'll hear it said they're too in love
parts.note: said aloud, 'too in love' is 'two in love': a pair of sweethearts going out together

explanation.surface: Gossip that some lovers are overdoing it, being far too smitten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You'll hear it said' tells you to take 'too' by its sound, as 'two': two people in love, wooing each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of sweethearts in the wooing stage are two people in love.

clue.text: Frank caught joiner with a little girl returning

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
and is a joining word, a conjunction

indicators.note: returning says the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, a diminutive of Diana

explanation.surface: A frank man is caught joining up with a small girl on her way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' sends the girl's name backwards; 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid and frank are synonyms for open and honest.

clue.text: Dangerous guns a felon keeps hidden

indicators.note: keeps hidden says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A criminal is concealing firearms, which is risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsafe is risky or perilous.

clue.text: Pipes rubbish container on board boat!

indicators.note: on board says one thing is placed inside another, as cargo inside a vessel

parts.note: a tug is a small boat that tows ships
a bin holds rubbish

explanation.surface: Plumbing pipes stored in a waste bin aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' puts the rubbish container inside the boat, as cargo sits in a hold; 'boat' is the towing vessel, not the outer container.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubing is a length or system of tubes, the same as pipes.

clue.text: Sends right sort of garment

indicators.note: sort of here means put in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dispatches the correct kind of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges SENDSRIGHT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a garment worn in bed.

clue.text: See 1
Table salesman to ring up telephonist

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole run is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a rota is a table of duties
rep is short for a sales representative
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A table-selling salesman phones the switchboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole of ROTAREPO round, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An operator is a person working a telephone switchboard.

clue.text: Six-footer is into plain tropical fruit

indicators.note: is into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an ant is an insect, with six legs

explanation.surface: A tall person is fond of simple exotic produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it means a six-legged insect, which 'is into' places within the plain word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantain is a banana-like fruit grown in the tropics.

clue.text: Backed tip, so red when it goes wrong!

parts.note: the tip of something is its end

indicators.note: something gone wrong is jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A betting tip was supported, so it's in the red after it failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it goes wrong' rearranges the letters of 'so red'; the betting surface hides that 'tip' just means an end.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse something is to support it, so backed is a synonym.

clue.text: Goes bang, damaging animal food containers

indicators.note: damaging suggests the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: the printed words supply the anagram fodder, with one letter wrong as printed

explanation.surface: Something explodes, wrecking the horses' feed bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaging' rearranges the fodder, but as printed GOESBANG has a G where the answer needs a second S: a slip by the setter or printer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosebags are feed bags hung over a horse's muzzle.

clue.text: Recompense retiring artist

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a drawer is one who draws

explanation.surface: Payment for an artist who is leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns DRAWER around.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a payment made in return for something, a recompense.

clue.text: Vastness of NY if travelling around in it

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround the words that follow
travelling suggests the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: How big New York seems if you travel around in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges the letters of NY and 'if', and 'around' wraps them about the words 'in it', which stay as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinity is boundless extent, endless vastness.

clue.text: Clergyman returns rubbish to fool

indicators.note: returns says the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
a sap is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: A clergyman sends back nonsense to an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ROTSAP round; 'to' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a minister in charge of a congregation.

clue.text: Soak and prime, stirring liquidising agent

indicators.note: stirring and liquidising both suggest mixing ingredients, so these letters are blended

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: steep and prepare, mixing the blending agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring liquidising' rearranges PRIMEAGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To impregnate is to saturate or permeate, as when one soaks something.

clue.text: People jump on one passenger vehicle taking home staff

parts.note: a tram carries passengers on rails

indicators.note: taking says one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: a staff is a pole
in means at home

explanation.surface: People leap onto a tram carrying office workers home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but it is a stick, and 'taking' has it hold 'home'. The definition describes what the answer is used for.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is a springy sheet that people bounce on.

clue.text: They take risks as they're strolling after midnight

indicators.note: after says the strollers come behind the midnight letter

parts.note: the middle letter of night is G
amblers are people who walk at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: Gamblers out walking late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' means the middle of the word night, its letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamblers are people who bet, taking chances.

clue.text: Try to prevent it going in reverse

indicators.note: going in says the word it is inserted inside the other piece

parts.note: to oppose something is to try to stop it

explanation.surface: Trying to stop a car going in reverse gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the definition, as a noun meaning the contrary; 'going in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The reverse of something is its contrary.

clue.text: Modified and now just needing two keys

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
E and D are musical keys

explanation.surface: Something was changed and now only needs two keys to open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keys' means musical keys, named by letters, not door keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusted means altered slightly, modified.

clue.text: Venomous creature ruined diarist's plant

parts.note: an asp is a poisonous snake

indicators.note: ruined says the letters are wrecked and reassembled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A poisonous snake wrecked a diary writer's houseplant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges the diarist's letters, the possessive S giving none. An aspidistra is a hardy, leafy houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspidistra is a leafy plant, popular indoors.

clue.text: Wrench artist dropped in drive

indicators.note: dropped in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a spin is a short drive in a car
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist dropped a spanner on the driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrench' suggests a spanner but means a twisted joint; 'dropped in' places the Royal Academician inside the drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is an injury to a joint, from a twist or wrench.

clue.text: After Los Angeles continue to saltwater lake

indicators.note: After says the second piece follows the first

parts.note: to go on is to continue

explanation.surface: Travel instructions: after LA, carry on to a coastal lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of salt water cut off from the sea by a reef or sandbank.

clue.text: Pinches less at dances

indicators.note: dances suggests the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone nicks fewer things at parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dances' rearranges LESSAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch is slang for to steal, so pinches means steals.

clue.text: Tongue of stout shoe

explanation.surface: The flap of a sturdy shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' suggests the flap of a shoe, but it means a language or accent; 'of' just links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue here is a regional accent, especially Irish; also a heavy leather shoe with decorative perforations.

clue.text: Aubergine seed factory

explanation.surface: An aubergine works as a factory for seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as two words: an egg is a seed, and a plant is a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggplant is the American name for an aubergine; also a works producing ova, which are seeds of a kind.

clue.text: Leaves about a quarter and survives

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: exits means goes out, leaves
S, south, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone goes out for a quarter of an hour and lives on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts S inside EXITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to live, to survive.

clue.text: Accountant's a bright star and an amorous man

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant, with the possessive S
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: An accountant is a shining star and a ladies' man.
explanation.walkthrough: Casanova was an 18th-century Venetian famous for his love affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Casanova is a womaniser, after a famous Venetian seducer.

clue.text: Firm dates arranged last July

indicators.note: arranged says the letters are put in a new order
last picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Fixed dates were set up last July.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges DATES into STEAD; 'last' takes Y from July.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady means stable and firm.

clue.text: Tastes some chicken joints Nina brought back in

indicators.note: in says the reversed name goes inside the joints

parts.note: chicken legs are joints of chicken

indicators.note: brought back says the name is read backwards

explanation.surface: Nina tries some chicken legs she brought home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' sends Nina's name backwards, and 'in' sets it within the chicken joints.
explanation.definitionFit: Leanings are inclinations, one's tastes or preferences.
